Slots.issue: NibbitsNormal.Slots => ["front", "back"] (NibbitsNormal.cs:13, backed by the private consts _backSlot/_frontSlot at :9-11). NIBBITS_NORMAL = Encounter(id='nibbits_normal', monster_classes=[partial(Nibbit, is_front=True), Nibbit]) declares no `slots=`/`monster_slots=` (both default to the empty tuple, sts2_rl/monsters/base.py), so CombatState.sort_enemies_by_slot_name (combat.py:1337-1357) is a permanent no-op for this encounter (combat.py:1349's `if encounter is None or not getattr(encounter, 'slots', ()): return`). DORMANT, not live: Nibbit.cs (read top to bottom) has no CreatureCmd.Add call anywhere -- BUTT/SLICE/HISS are its only three moves, none of which summon, and Nibbit has no other spawn path in this or any other C# file (grep of `CreatureCmd.Add<Nibbit>` across src/ returns only NibbitsNormal.GenerateMonsters itself). SortEnemiesBySlotName's only OTHER caller (CombatManager.AddCreature, gated on a non-null SlotName) is therefore never reached again after the initial construction, so the game's own ordering is fixed at construction time and never re-sorted either. The sim's construction order ([front-tagged Nibbit, plain Nibbit], nibbit.py:62) already matches the game's array order ([front,back], NibbitsNormal.cs:25-29) without needing the slot tags or the sort. Executed: `py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e1.py nibbits-slot-dormancy` confirms zero `CreatureCmd.add`/`CreatureCmd.Add` occurrences in the Nibbit class body on either side. Mechanism id: encounter/nibbits_normal/g1. Filed as a real structural gap (the sim genuinely cannot express this encounter's slot row, and a future summon-capable Nibbit variant or a shared Slots-reading feature would reopen it instantly) but not live today.

RoomType.rationale: NibbitsNormal.RoomType => RoomType.Monster (NibbitsNormal.cs:15). Sim carries no room_type field on the Encounter dataclass; 'nibbits_normal' is placed in rooms.py:148-153's normal_keys for _overgrowth_rooms() (seam/rooms_and_map owns the picker itself). GOLD_REWARD_RANGES[RoomType.MONSTER]=(10,20) (rewards.py:171) matches EncounterModel.cs:70/89's Monster=>10/20 defaults, which NibbitsNormal does not override.

HasScene.rationale: Selects a bespoke Godot scene layout for this encounter (public bool => true) instead of the act's generic combat scene. Its only reader is NCombatRoom.cs:289, Godot scene instantiation -- zero gameplay effect. The headless sim renders no scene.

AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: No sim counterpart. C#'s only consumers of AllPossibleMonsters are ActModel.AllMonsters (ActModel.cs:169, read only by ModelDb.Monsters -> UnlockConsoleCmd.cs:68/147's dev-console 'monsters' listing and NGeneralStatsGrid.cs:164's stats-screen ratio label) and the Bestiary screen (NBestiary.cs:194) -- all UI/dev-console, zero gameplay or RNG effect, confirmed by reading every caller in src/. The headless sim has neither surface, so omitting a counterpart costs nothing observable.

GenerateMonsters.issue: Roster (2x Nibbit), order ([front-tagged, plain] on both sides) and draw count (0 == 0) all match; only the SLOT half of each tuple diverges. NibbitsNormal.GenerateMonsters (NibbitsNormal.cs:21-30) returns [(front-nibbit,"front"),(plain-nibbit,"back")] -- tagged tuples. NIBBITS_NORMAL.monster_slots is unset (default (), sts2_rl/monsters/base.py), so the sim's two Nibbits carry slot_name=None on construction. Same mechanism and same dormancy reasoning as the Slots entry above (encounter/nibbits_normal/g1): nothing in Nibbit.cs ever reads or re-sorts on SlotName after construction, so the missing tags are inert given the order already matches. Filed for completeness per the audit brief's instruction to verdict the slot-name half of GenerateMonsters explicitly, not folded silently into the roster/order verdict.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.maps_to: (structural -- Encounter dataclass has no hook methods)
ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: EncounterModel.ShouldReceiveCombatHooks => false (EncounterModel.cs:39), not overridden by NibbitsNormal. The sim's Encounter dataclass (sts2_rl/monsters/base.py) declares no hook methods and is never passed to HookSystem.register -- it is plain data, structurally incapable of joining the hook walk, which reproduces 'the encounter itself is not a listener' exactly.

guards.what: MinGoldReward/MaxGoldReward gold ladder (the encounter brief's 5th thing to verdict)
guards.rationale: NibbitsNormal does not override MinGoldReward/MaxGoldReward, so both inherit EncounterModel.cs:64-100's RoomType ladder (Monster=10-20) times AscensionHelper.PovertyAscensionGoldMultiplier under AscensionLevel.Poverty. NIBBITS_NORMAL carries min_gold=None, max_gold=None (Encounter dataclass default, sts2_rl/monsters/base.py), so rewards.py:886-887 falls back to GOLD_REWARD_RANGES[RoomType.MONSTER]=(10,20) (rewards.py:171) -- the same ladder. Ascension (Poverty) scaling is out of scope by the audit contract (rewards.py:32's explicit 'no Scarcity/Poverty scaling').

guards.what: EncounterModel.Rng independence (per the encounter brief: verify the sim does not draw encounter rolls off a shared/run-level stream)
guards.rationale: NibbitsNormal.GenerateMonsters makes zero base.Rng calls (NibbitsNormal.cs:21-30, confirmed by reading the whole method) and the sim's create_monsters counterpart (the default Encounter.create_monsters this unit inherits, sts2_rl/monsters/base.py) makes zero calls to any Rng/random.Random for composition -- there is nothing here for stream identity to diverge on. (Draw-count fact only; which named stream backs EncounterModel.Rng in general is seam/rng_streams' mechanism, already verdicted faithful for the seeding formula at rng_streams step 21.)
